text: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) acts as a lysosomotropic weak base that accumulates within acidic endolysosomal compartments, where it elevates intralysosomal pH and disrupts the conformational maturation of Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9). By interfering with the proteolytic cleavage required for TLR9 activation, HCQ prevents the receptor from binding to self-nucleic acid-IgG immune complexes, thereby inhibiting the downstream signaling cascade (MyD88-IRF7) that drives the excessive production of Type I interferons. In Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), this blockade effectively dampens the chronic innate immune activation and autoantibody production characteristic of the disease, providing a foundational therapeutic strategy to reduce flares and improve long-term survival.
